title: Cold Email Tools for Agencies — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Best Cold Email Tools for Agencies
description: Instantly, lemlist, and Smartlead compared for agencies running cold email for clients: prices, sending accounts, client workspaces, and HubSpot connections.
h1: Cold email tools for an agency running outbound for clients
dek: Three cold email platforms an agency can run several client programs on.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This page is for a small agency that runs cold email on behalf of clients: you write the sequences, manage the sending domains, and report on replies. Some clients want the replies to land in their {{link:hubspot}} account, and some don't have a CRM at all.

An agency needs different things from a cold email tool than an in-house rep does. You need lots of sending accounts, a clean way to keep clients apart, and a reporting story you can hand to someone who isn't in the tool.

Pick Instantly if your main cost is sending accounts and you want them unlimited on one plan. Pick lemlist if your campaigns run across email and other channels and the client's team wants to log in too. Pick Smartlead if keeping each client in its own branded workspace matters most.
Whatever you pick, the tool won't fix deliverability on its own. Separate domains per client, warmed-up inboxes, and sane daily volumes do more for reply rates than any feature on these pages.

Instantly's Growth plan is {{fact:instantly.growth_price}}, with {{fact:instantly.unlimited_accounts}}. Instantly also sells larger bundles that add data credits and higher sending volume; check the pricing page for the current mix. Per Instantly, {{fact:instantly.automations}}.

lemlist's email plan is {{fact:lemlist.email_price}}, and the multichannel plan is {{fact:lemlist.multichannel_price}}. Billing is {{fact:lemlist.billing}}. The email plan comes with {{fact:lemlist.unlimited_senders}}. There's a {{fact:lemlist.trial}}.
On HubSpot, lemlist {{fact:lemlist.hubspot_sync}}. Its help center notes it {{fact:lemlist.hubspot_plans}}, so a client on free HubSpot is out of luck.

Smartlead's Base plan is {{fact:smartlead.base_price}}, and Pro is {{fact:smartlead.pro_price}}. For agencies, {{fact:smartlead.whitelabel}}, and {{fact:smartlead.prime_clients}}. It offers {{fact:smartlead.no_lockin}}.
Smartlead has {{fact:smartlead.hubspot}}. One catch from its help center: {{fact:smartlead.hubspot_per_campaign}}.

Start from your client count and how separate they need to be. If clients never log in, a single account with good tagging may be enough. If clients want their own login and your brand on it, workspaces and white-labeling move to the top of the list.
Then look at which clients run HubSpot on a paid plan. lemlist needs a paid HubSpot plan, and Smartlead's sync has to be set per campaign, so map that out before the first client goes live.
Last, price the seat count you'll really have. Unlimited users or unlimited sending accounts matter more for an agency than the entry price on the page.
Agree with the client on who owns the sending domains and who sees the replies. Write that down. It's the first thing that becomes a problem when a client leaves.
Run a small test campaign from each new domain before the full send, and check that replies and meetings show up where the client expects them, whether that's HubSpot or a shared inbox.

Smartlead's Base plan is {{fact:smartlead.base_price}}. Instantly's Growth plan is {{fact:instantly.growth_price}}. lemlist's email plan is {{fact:lemlist.email_price}}.

closing: For an agency, pick the tool that keeps clients cleanly apart and gets replies into each client's system without a custom build every time.

Sending accounts.smartlead: Volume is set by plan: Base covers 6,000 email sends.
